To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

it is possible, in theory and in simulations, to learn the transformation from time series in low dimensional observables to molecular configurations and to use this transformation to reconstruct protein structures from synthetic time series in experimentable molecular distances.

we have established a theoretical framework and algorithmic approach to reconstruct the instantaneous protein structures from time-series of experimentally measurable observable such as intramolecule distances, and demonstrated its accuracy in simulations of a polymer chain and the chignolin protein.
we have developed a new approach to reconstruct protein structure from experimental time series data that combines tools from manifold learning, neural networks, and molecular dynamics.

the development of new methods for the study of the dynamics of biomolecules, with particular emphasis on protein folding.
the development and application of mathematical tools for the analysis and reconstruction of single molecule time series data.

we developed a novel approach to learn the transformation from time series in observable quantities to molecular configuration and validated it with simulations.
it is possible, in principle, to use the information contained in single molecule time series to reconstruct molecular configurations, and that we have developed an algorithm to do so in practice.

we developed a new method to reconstruct molecular configurations of proteins and polymers from time series data in experimentally measurable quantities, and demonstrated the method on synthetic data from molecular dynamics simulations.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in the absence of any prior information about the system, it is possible to learn the transformation that maps a low dimensional representation of a molecular time series to the full molecular configuration.
the Takens delay embedding theorem can be used to learn the transformation from low dimensional time series in experimentable observables to the high dimensional configuration of the system.
the reconstruction of molecular configurations from time traces of experimental observables is possible in principle and can be achieved with high fidelity.
